final_message:
The bug was an off-by-one in `record_failure` in `billing/dunning.py`. I fixed it, and the reproduction test now passes along with the rest of the suite (25 passed). I ran the reproduction as a temporary test and removed it afterwards, so it isn't in the suite.

`record_failure` checked `attempt_count < len(offsets)`. With `retry_offsets_days: [1]`, the first failed charge at subscribe time already counted as the last attempt. The final action ran immediately, which tried an invalid `active` → `unpaid` transition. It also meant the configured retry never happened.

I changed the check to `<=`, so each offset schedules a retry after the initial attempt. The failed charge now schedules a retry and moves the subscription to `past_due`. After the cancel, the retry on day 1 fails and exhausts the policy. The subscription is already canceled by then, so the invoice is marked uncollectible, as the test expects.

I wrote `answer.json` with `{"file": "dunning.py", "function": "record_failure"}`. It's listed in `.gitignore`, so it won't show up in `git status`.

steps.command: cd billing && sed -n 20,60p dunning.py; sed -n 25,50p engine.py; sed -n 135,160p subscriptions.py

cd /tmp/bsvc-604247a5/billing-service; cat >> tests/test_tmp.py <<'E'


def test_retries_exhausted_after_cancel_marks_uncollectible():
    from conftest import World

    w = World({"retry_offsets_days": [1], "final_action": "mark_unpaid"})
    cus = w.customer(last4="0002")
    sub = w.engine.subscribe(cus["id"], [(w.monthly["id"], 1)])
    w.engine.cancel(sub["id"], at_period_end=False)
    w.advance_days(1)
    [inv] = w.engine.invoices_for(cus["id"])
    assert sub["status"] == "canceled"
    assert inv["status"] == "uncollectible"
E
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q tests/test_tmp.py 2>&1 | grep -B30 Error | head -60; grep -n "record_failure" -r billing

cd /tmp/bsvc-604247a5/billing-service; python3 - <<'E'
p='billing/dunning.py'
s=open(p).read()
s=s.replace('''    else:
        transition(ctx, subscription, "unpaid")''','''    else:
        if subscription["status"] != "past_due":
            transition(ctx, subscription, "past_due")
        transition(ctx, subscription, "unpaid")''')
open(p,'w').write(s)
E
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q 2>&1 | tail -15

cd /tmp/bsvc-604247a5/billing-service; git checkout billing/dunning.py
sed -i 's/if invoice\["attempt_count"\] < len(offsets):/if invoice["attempt_count"] <= len(offsets):/' billing/dunning.py
rm tests/test_tmp.py
echo '{"file": "dunning.py", "function": "record_failure"}' > answer.json
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q 2>&1 | tail -5
cat >> tests/test_tmp.py <<'E'
E
rm tests/test_tmp.py; git status --short

cd /tmp/bsvc-604247a5/billing-service; cat > tests/test_tmp.py <<'E'
def test_retries_exhausted_after_cancel_marks_uncollectible():
    from conftest import World

    w = World({"retry_offsets_days": [1], "final_action": "mark_unpaid"})
    cus = w.customer(last4="0002")
    sub = w.engine.subscribe(cus["id"], [(w.monthly["id"], 1)])
    w.engine.cancel(sub["id"], at_period_end=False)
    w.advance_days(1)
    [inv] = w.engine.invoices_for(cus["id"])
    assert sub["status"] == "canceled"
    assert inv["status"] == "uncollectible"
E
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q 2>&1 | tail -8; rm tests/test_tmp.py; git status --short
cd /tmp/bsvc-604247a5/billing-service; cat answer.json; git check-ignore -v answer.json
